source_text: Salvator cognoscebat seipsum factum ex semine David secundum carnem, praedestinatum Filium Dei in virtute; Ego sum via, veritas et vita; ante Abraham ego sum; Verbum quod erat in principio apud Deum. Pharisaei sciebant quod secundum dispensationem humanam de semine David erat, profundiora vero nesciebant. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: Christ's self-knowledge and the Pharisees' ignorance
orientation: Origen is explaining what Jesus knew about himself as Son of David according to the flesh and Son of God in power, in contrast to what the Pharisees knew.
pass_a_gloss: Savior knew himself made from seed of David according to flesh, predestined Son of God in power; I am way, truth and life; before Abraham I am; Word which was in beginning with God. Pharisees knew that according to dispensation human from seed of David he was, deeper [things] but not they knew. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.term: factum ex semine David secundum carnem
choices.english: made from the seed of David according to the flesh
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of factum and the Pauline phrasing of Romans 1:3, which Origen is echoing.
rejected: born of David's line according to the flesh
descended from David in the flesh

choices.english: predestined Son of God in power
choices.why: Preserves the exact Pauline wording from Romans 1:4, including the passive participle and the phrase 'in power.'
rejected: designated Son of God in power
appointed Son of God with power

choices.why: Renders the technical term dispensatio literally, keeping Origen's distinction between the human economy and the deeper divine reality.
Keeps the comparative force of the neuter plural, matching Origen's contrast between surface knowledge and deeper spiritual knowledge.

Ego sum via, veritas et vita

pass_b_english: The Savior knew himself to be made from the seed of David according to the flesh, predestined Son of God in power (Romans 1:3-4); he knew himself as “I am the way, and the truth, and the life” (John 14:6), as “before Abraham was, I am” (John 8:58), as the Word who was in the beginning with God (John 1:1). The Pharisees knew that according to the human dispensation he was from the seed of David, but they did not know the deeper things. Glory to Christ. Amen.
